// The twin of stdlib/internal/bytealg/native.gp for real Go (tests/twin_test.go): the routines that
// gocpp has in C++ are the public functions of bytes and strings, which compute the same results. A
// test that says "// std-internal:" and passes with this file and with gocpp's C++ has the same
// output from both, so its // Output: block is what Go computes.

package bytealg

import (
	"bytes"
	"strings"
)

func IndexByte(b []byte, c byte) int             { return bytes.IndexByte(b, c) }
func IndexByteString(s string, c byte) int       { return strings.IndexByte(s, c) }
func LastIndexByte(s []byte, c byte) int         { return bytes.LastIndexByte(s, c) }
func LastIndexByteString(s string, c byte) int   { return strings.LastIndexByte(s, c) }
func Count(b []byte, c byte) int                 { return bytes.Count(b, []byte{c}) }
func CountString(s string, c byte) int           { return strings.Count(s, string([]byte{c})) }
func Equal(a, b []byte) bool                     { return bytes.Equal(a, b) }
func Compare(a, b []byte) int                    { return bytes.Compare(a, b) }
func CompareString(a, b string) int              { return strings.Compare(a, b) }
func Index(a, b []byte) int                      { return bytes.Index(a, b) }
func IndexString(a, b string) int                { return strings.Index(a, b) }
func MakeNoZero(n int) []byte                    { return make([]byte, n) }
